getting-started.text: If the player does not have the requirements to begin the quest:

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Ahhh, good day young adventurer. I can't stop to talk right now I'm afraid.
You do not meet all of the requirements to start the Grim Tales quest.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Ahhh, good day young adventurer. A good day indeed! Sylas is the name. It is lucky for you that you met me.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Well it just so happens, [player name], that I have something you simply must have!

getting-started.player: Why would I want beans exactly? I mean, beans are good, of course, but I'm pretty sure I can get them anywhere.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Ahhh, but not beans like this, young [player name]. No, not at all! These are 'magic' beans.

getting-started.player: Ok then. So what do they do exactly?

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: An excellent question! Excellent indeed! What do they do? What do they do? Yes, yes! A most excellent question!

getting-started.player: O...kay. So, are you going to tell me what they do?

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: You must plant them in the ground. Water them well. Then the magic will work, it's...er...magic...yes! Plant them, [player name].

getting-started.player: So, can I have the beans then?

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: All in good time, my excitable young friend. All in good time.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Few things in this world are free, you know, and beans - magical or otherwise - are no exception!

getting-started.player: So, how much gold do you want for the beans, if I decide to buy them?

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Ah, well you see now I am a collector of rare and unusual trinkets and objects. Not much in value, but very important to me.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Right, well I think that for magic beans, I will need something magical back and I know of just the right items that would help my collection.

getting-started.player: Ok, so if I get these items, you will trade them for the beans. Is that right?

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Yes! Excellent! You do catch on quick! I can see that we will become great business partners indeed. Oh, yes. Yes indeed! Hmm-ha! Yes.

getting-started.player: What items do you need me to find then - assuming I still want those beans of course. Not that I do, but I might.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: Well, there are two. The first item should be nice and simple for you to get for me. I want a griffin feather. Now, this is not just any feather, this one is special.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: There is a griffin named Grimgnash who lives in a nest on one of the peaks of White Wolf Mountain. It is one of his feathers that I want.

getting-started.speaker: Sylas
getting-started.text: But although this task should be easy, you must be careful [player name]. Grimgnash has a very bad temper and even sharper claws!

options.text: What do you need the feather for?

steps.player: What do you need the feather for?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: I told you, [player name]. It is for my collection of magical items and trinkets, weird and wonderful thereof.

steps.player: Thereof?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Yes, I was quite happy with that word. I think it went rather well in that last sentence, don't you?

steps.player: I guess. If you say so.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Yes. Excellent! Yes. Now...er...was there anything else?

options.text: How do I find Grimgnash again?

steps.player: How do I find Grimgnash again?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: When he's not chewing on some poor soul's bones or raining terror on an unsuspecting village, he can be found in his nest, atop White Wolf Mountain.

steps.player: Excuse me...say what now? He chews people's bones? I thought you said this was an easy task?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Oh, I daresay he has to eat sometimes. But I don't think he'd take too much fancy for you. Not much meat on you at all. Oh dear me, no!

steps.player: You know, I'm not sure that was even a compliment.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: I'm sure it was meant to be! Don't worry, [player name], you'll be fine. Now was there anything else?

options.text: What's the other item I need to find?

steps.player: What's the other item I need to find?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Right, well, the second item is this. I know of a dwarf named Rupert the Beard who has a very fine dwarven helmet. I'd like you to see if you can obtain it for me.

steps.player: Ok. Where can I find him?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Travel north-east from here and between the Goblin Village and Ice Mountain you will find Rupert in a tower there.

steps.player: Ok, that seems simple enough. I'll get the helmet for you as well.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Excellent! Yes, yes. Now was there anything else?

options.text: Do you have any weird items in your collection?

steps.player: Do you have any weird items in your collection?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Haha! Weird items? Oh yes. Yes indeed! Yes. Many items. Many items. Yes.

steps.player: Umm...I see. Well, can you tell me about any of them?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Hmm. Well let's see now. I have the second eye of a mutant two-eyed cyclops. That was a rare find indeed! And at a tidy price too!

steps.player: A two-eyed cyclops? Uh...wouldn't that be a normal giant perhaps?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Whatever do you mean? How many mutant two-eyed cyclops do you think there are out there? Not many, I'd wager!

steps.player: Umm...no, I guess not. Well, what else do you have?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Ah, well I'm glad you asked. My most prized possession to date: Through my connections, I managed to acquire a horn-less Unicorn!

steps.player: Really? That's amazing! A unicorn without a horn?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Yes. Yes indeed! Indeed yes! And I'm very proud of it, too! It was an exceptionally lucky find, I must say!

steps.player: I expect so. Well, on to other things for now then, I guess.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Of course. Was there anything else you wanted?

options.text: I should be off, I think.

steps.player: I should be off, I think.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Excellent, excellent! Best of luck then, my friend. I'll be right here waiting for you to return.

steps.player: I have come for your magic feather!

steps.speaker: Grimgnash

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-putting-gr.speaker: Grimgnash
obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-putting-gr.text: Hmm. When Grimgnash little grifflet, Grimgnash's mother-griff used to tell bedtime story to Grimgnash. That always help Grimgnash sleep.

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-putting-gr.player: So you want me to tell you a bed-time story, is that right?
Right, well I'm sure that shouldn't be too hard. I know lots of stories!

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-putting-gr.speaker: Grimgnash

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-putting-gr.player: Death and fire?...ok then. Let me see...

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-putting-gr.speaker: Grimgnash
obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-putting-gr.text: And make story good. Otherwise, if no sleep, Grimgnash more hungry!

steps.speaker: Grimgnash

options.text: Skullrot was insane!

steps.player: Skullrot was insane!

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Yes, insane! Grimgnash like that word! Grimgnash mother always say Grimgnash's daddy insane. Grimgnash's daddy eat own claws. Grimgnash laughed.
Grimgnash cackles in what you can only imagine must be a griffin's laugh.

steps.player: That's...lovely. Uh...shall I continue?

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Yes! Grimgnash liking this story now! Go on!

steps.player: Ok, then. So Skullrot was completely insane. He was off his rocker. One noodle short of a bowl of spaghetti. Not quite all there.
Anyway, he was out haunting his graveyard one day when he came across a small gnome.

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Grimgnash not like gnomes. They stringy and chewy and they not have much meat for Grimgnash's belly.

steps.player: Uh, I'm sorry to hear that. Anyway, this poor gnome had somehow got his foot stuck under a fallen gravestone.

options.text: Skullrot lifted the gravestone off.

steps.player: Skullrot lifted the gravestone off.
And the gnome ran away as quick as his little feet could carry him.

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: What?! Gnome snack gets away? That dumb. How Skullrot eat? Stupid human can't tell good story!

steps.player: No, wait...!

steps.text: (Grimgnash attacks the player, and does a large amount of damage.)
Grimgnash lashes out at you and you recoil backwards in pain. You must be more careful what you say. Grimgnash could eat you at any moment!

options.text: Skullrot left the gnome there to die.

steps.player: Skullrot left the gnome there to die.
So the gnome, thinking this was his chance, found a log to lever the stone off his foot and he scarpered away quickly.

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: What?! Gnome snack gets away? That stupid. That not good story! Grimgnash only feel more hungry now!

steps.player: No, wait, I got it wrong! Wait...!

steps.text: (Grimgnash attacks the player, and does a large amount of damage.)
Grimgnash lashes out at you and you recoil backwards in pain. You must be more careful what you say. Grimgnash could eat you at any moment!

options.text: Skullrot laughed at the gnome.

steps.player: Skullrot laughed at the gnome.
In fact, he laughed so hard that he fell backwards into an empty grave and was never seen again. The end.

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Graah! That good stor...wait. What happen to gnome?

steps.player: Eh? Oh, uh...well without Skullrot there he was able to get himself free again and ran away, vowing never to return to the graveyard ever again.

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: What?! Little bite-size gnome runs away? That not good ending! Gnome should be mashed by something like...something like Grimgnash! Stupid human get eaten now!

steps.player: No, wait, I got it wrong! Wait...!

steps.text: (Grimgnash attacks the player, and does a large amount of damage.)
Grimgnash lashes out at you and you recoil backwards in pain. You must be more careful what you say. Grimgnash could eat you at any moment!

options.text: Skullrot hungrily grabbed the gnome's hair.

steps.player: Skullrot hungrily grabbed the gnome's hair.
Skullrot wrenched the gnome out with one hand, pulling hard on his hair. The poor gnome's foot snapped out of the gravestone and went crack as his foot dislocated!

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Raahahaha! Stupid gnome! Serves gnome right for being stringy and chewy! What happen next?

steps.player: Well, the poor gnome - Nobby was his name - was in terrible pain and fear as to what would happen to him next.

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Grimgnash not care what gnome's name is. Grimgnash not give food names. Does human call a carrot Jasper or something? Tell rest of story!

steps.player: Ok, ok. Anyway, the gnome was in awful pain, so Skullrot took him back to his home in his grave where he...

options.text: Locked him in an iron cage.

steps.player: Locked him in an iron cage.
Luckily, the bars were built for a human sized person and so the gnome quickly slipped through them and ran - painfully - out the door.
The gnome headed straight out the graveyard, glad to still be alive and never wanting to return.

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Stringy gnome gets away? Stupid human make Grimgnash more hungry with story like that!

steps.player: No, stop! Arrgh...!

steps.text: (Grimgnash attacks the player, and does a large amount of damage.)

options.text: Put him into a pot for dinner.

steps.player: Put him into a pot for dinner.
Skullrot was making a stew and had decided that the gnome would taste wonderful in it.

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Ah! Grimgnash likes gnome stew. Just like Grimgnash used to eat at home. Mmmm!

steps.player: However, Skullrot had filled the pot up too much, and so while the skeleton's back was turned, the gnome swam to the edge of the pot and up, over the side.
With a little shout of glee, the gnome hopped on one leg straight out of the door and fled as fast as his little foot could hop him!

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Gnome gets away? What kind of story that? Grimgnash think he eat human now!

steps.player: Argh...!

options.text: Started to strangle the poor gnome.

steps.player: Started to strangle the poor gnome.
The gnome struggled with the cold boney fingers that were trying to end his life until he managed to pry himself free!

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Ohhh! This getting good! Grimgnash like this. (Yawn!) Grimgnash feels sleepy.

steps.player: Ok, it was all the little gnome could do to crawl painfully across the floor away from Skullrot, who was busy getting a pot to put the gnome in.
Then, when all seemed lost for the little gnome, he suddenly saw something that might save his little life!

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Grargh! What? What? What little gnome see? He must not escape! Grimgnash hungry to think of it!

steps.player: Ok, ok! Don't worry, we're almost done.

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Grmmm. Good. Grimgnash getting sleepy...(yawn).
It looks like Grimgnash is almost asleep. You better think about the best way to finish this story!

steps.player: So, then. The gnome looked up and he saw what might be his best chance to get out alive!

options.text: He saw a hole he could just fit through.

steps.player: He saw a hole he could just fit through.
As he crawled forward two yellow slitted eyes appeared in the gloom before him. He froze in fear!
Skullrot did not get his dinner that night, but something else...something much worse...did. The end.
So what did you think, Grimgnash?

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Zzzzzz....zzzz....zzz...
It looks like that did the trick. Grimgnash is snoring loudly! You better grab the feather and get out before he wakes up again!

options.text: He saw a big axe leaning on the wall.

steps.player: He saw a big axe leaning on the wall.
He crawled painfully, oh so painfully over to the axe. He could use it to kill Skullrot.
As he grasped the axe he realised it was a lot heavier than it looked! In fact much heavier indeed! He couldn't hold it or stop it falling off the wall!
SCHNUNK!!

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: What happened? Human tell Grimgnash!

steps.player: As the axe fell, the poor gnome could not get out of the way in time and the razor sharp blade fell CRACK! And it killed him instantly.
And so Skullrot was pleased to find that he had a nice dinner for that night and sat down for a big supper! The end.
What did you think, Grimgnash?

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Zzzzzz....zzzz....zzz...
It looks like that did the trick. Grimgnash is snoring loudly! You better grab the feather and get out before he wakes up again!

options.text: He saw some bones lying in the corner.

steps.player: He saw some bones lying in the corner.
He quickly remembered that if he buried them he could get his prayer up and so might be able to cast a heal spell on his legs!
He dragged his painful body over to the bones and buried them all - there was quite a large pile - in the floor.
All of a sudden, he remembered a good spell to heal himself from his injuries. He started to recite the prayer quickly.
Just then, a huge zombie appeared out of nowhere and mumbled something about his bones being disturbed! The zombie crunched his fist down on the gnome's head.
The gnome cried out in terror and realised that all was lost! He could not get away now!
And so, Skullrot decided to invite the zombie to dinner as he never usually had guests.
Then the two of them laughed and joked merrily throughout the night with their stomachs full of a hearty dinner! The end.
So what did you think, Grimgnash?

steps.speaker: Grimgnash
steps.text: Zzzzzz....zzzz....zzz...
It looks like that did the trick. Grimgnash is snoring loudly! You better grab the feather and get out before he wakes up again!

options.text: He saw a small sandwich on the floor.

steps.player: He saw a small sandwich on the floor.
He pulled himself over to it. In his desperation he thought to himself, there's a sandwich here. A sandwich! Maybe the skeleton will eat that instead?
He quickly grasped the sandwich in his little hands. Strangely, in his panic-stricken state, he noticed that it was long and tubular shaped.
What an odd thing to notice, he thought. And then all of a sudden he heard an almighty voice boom out of nowhere!
'SANDWICHES!!!'
'Oi!', said the voice. 'I didn't say you could take that!' And with that, there was an almighty crunch on his little gnome head, and that was the last thing he felt.
Skullrot sat down for the night and had a lovely big dinner, followed by many baguette sandwiches. Not triangle ones, no, no! The end.
What did you think, Grimgnash?

steps.player: Locked the gnome in the attic to die.
Fortunately for the gnome, Skullrot forgot that he lived in a grave, so he didn't have an attic. Instead the gnome was locked outside.
The gnome quickly limped away, glad to still be alive.

steps.player: There once was a little bunny called Flumper.

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-taking-the.text: You quickly take a feather while Grimgnash is sleeping.
If the player already owns a Griffin feather:

steps.text: You already have a feather from Grimgnash's nest. You don't need another one.

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-trying-to-.text: Grimgnash looks like he's sleeping nicely. It would probably be dangerous to your health to try and wake him up now!

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-giving-syl.player: Hi, Sylas. I have Grimgnash's feather for you.

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-giving-syl.speaker: Sylas
obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-giving-syl.text: Ah! Good work. Let me take that from you then.

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-giving-syl.speaker: Sylas
obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-giving-syl.text: I still need you to find Rupert the Beard's Helmet for me.

obtaining-grimgnash-s-feather-giving-syl.player: I have a question or two I would like to ask you.

options.text: What's the other item I need to find?
Do you have any weird items in your collection?
I should be off, I think.

entering-the-tower-attempting-to-enter-t.text: This door appears to be securely locked.

entering-the-tower-attempting-to-enter-t.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-attempting-to-enter-t.text: Excuse me. You can't go in there.

entering-the-tower-talking-to-miazrqa-be.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-talking-to-miazrqa-be.text: Who am I? Why, how impertinent! I am a princess and I will be spoken to like one. Now be off with you. I have no time for scruffy adventurers like yourself!

entering-the-tower-using-any-item-on-mia.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-using-any-item-on-mia.text: I'm pretty sure I don't want that.

entering-the-tower-using-any-item-on-mia.player: Well it's mine and you can't have it anyway. So there!

entering-the-tower-trying-to-climb-the-c.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-trying-to-climb-the-c.text: Hey, what's that noise over there? Is someone there? Who's near my tower?

entering-the-tower-trying-to-climb-the-c.player: Uh...no...no, nothing to see here. It was just the...er...wind! Yes, the wind.

entering-the-tower-trying-to-climb-the-c.text: It looks like you will need a Thieving level of 58 to climb over this wall without being seen.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-th.text: If the player hasn't spoken to Rupert before starting the quest:

steps.player: Hello there!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: I say! Where on Gielinor did that voice come from?

steps.player: Uh...hello there! Can you hear me?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Why yes. Yes I can. My word. Is that...is that one of the gods? Guthix perhaps? Saradomin?

steps.player: No, no. I'm not either of them.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Egad! You're not...Zamorak...are you? I mean, uh...begging your pardon of course, my Lord. No offence intended!

steps.player: Ha ha! No, I'm speaking to you through the pipe here! I'm at the bottom of your tower.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Oh. Oh I see! Oh, yes. How clever! Remarkable idea! However did you think of that? Good show, old bean!

steps.player: Who are you?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Rupert the Beard. At your service, old fruit.

steps.player: Rupert the Beard?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Yes, old ogleroot! On account of my wonderfully long bearded chin, you see.

steps.player: So what are you doing up there exactly? And how come you talk so strangely?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: What am I doing? Well, I guess I'm stuck in a matter of speaking. Dear me, yes! I'm stuck. And I speak in the King's speech, I'll have you know.

steps.player: Really? Which king?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Which K...? Why, THE King old spud! THE King! Only one worth mentioning in my opinion.

steps.player: Hey, you're not related to Sir Tiffy by any chance are you?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: What? That namby pamby nincompoop? Not on your nelly! More fluff in the ears than sense, that man!

steps.player: I see. Well is there anything I can do to help you up there?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: By Guthix, I know how you can help me!

steps.player: Sure. What can I do?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Hey, what's that noise over there? Is someone there?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Ye gods! We can't talk like this anymore. You need to find a way up to speak to me privately, old boot!

steps.player: Why? I don't understand what's going on!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: That woman is a princess. She's holding me prisoner. If she sees you I will be in even more trouble and who knows what she'll do to you!

steps.player: Right! Let me have a think, then!

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-th.text: If the player has previously spoken to Rupert before starting the quest:

steps.player: Hello there!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: I say! Where on Gielinor did that voice come from?

steps.player: Umm...it's me again. [player name]. I'm speaking in the drain pipe, remember?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Drain pi...oh, yes! Of course! Well, hello again old cigar! How great to se...er...hear from you again.

steps.player: I'm sure there must be something I can do to help you up there.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Hmm. Let me think now.

steps.player: Sure. What can I do?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Hey, what's that noise over there? Is someone there?

steps.player: Why? I don't understand what's going on!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: That woman is a princess. She's holding me prisoner. If she sees you I will be in even more trouble and who knows what she'll do to you!

steps.player: Right! Let me have a think, then!
I think I might have an idea!

entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.text: You there! Young scrub! Was that you making all that noise back there? Well? Speak up now.

entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.player: Noise? What noise? I didn't hear any noise.

entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.text: Well I distinctly heard voices at least! In any case, keep away from my tower.

entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.player: You're not very nice, are you?

entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.text: I am a princess. I don't have to be nice.

entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.player: I thought princesses were usually kind and loving and graceful?

entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.text: Ha! This isn't a fairytale, you know. This is rea...well, it's life!

entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.player: I see. Well I think I had better go then.

entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-speaking-with-miazrqa.text: Yes, and stay away from my dwar...uh...tower!

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-ag.player: I think I might have an idea!

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-ag.speaker: Drain pipe
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-ag.text: Jolly good show, old bean! What do you suggest?

options.text: You could try and climb down.

steps.player: You could try and climb down.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Climb down? What what what? It's miles! People are like little ants from up here...oh wait...no that's just a line of ants on the wall.

steps.player: It's really not that far.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Tish, posh and nonsense! You and your gangly long legs might be fine, but we dwarves are of shorter, stockier breed, old toothbrush!

steps.player: So you won't try it then?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Indeed, definitely and most indubitably not! Think of something else!

steps.player: Right...

options.text: I could try and climb up.

steps.player: I could try and climb up.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Hmm, a worthy endeavour I would say. Possibly with its merits. Yes, indeed. Now how will you get up here?

options.text: I could try and climb the walls.

steps.player: I could try and climb the walls.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: I don't know if that would work, old trousers. These walls are made from very smooth and flat stone. Excellent workmanship. Simply excellent.

steps.player: I'm glad you're able to admire the architecture, but you're still stuck up there!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Right you are, old pockets! Keep thinking! These are excellent ideas you're having!

options.text: Is there anything up there that can help?

steps.player: Is there anything up there that can help?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Not really, old spoon. There's not much up here except for me and my beard. Ha ha!

steps.player: Wait! That's it!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: What's it, old banana?

steps.player: I can't believe I'm going to say this, but...Rupert, Rupert, let down your beard!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Eh? Let down my beard? Have you lost it down there, old chum? Going a bit loopy?

steps.player: No, I mean hang your beard down over the tower and I'll climb up it, ok?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Ah ha ha! Excellent idea, old tomato! Here it comes then!
Rupert's beard is let down.

options.text: I can fly!

steps.player: I can fly!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: By Guthix and Saradomin, that's astounding! You are an absolute marvel! Can you really fly?

steps.player: Well...er...no, sorry, I made that last bit up!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: I see. Not very sporting in the circumstances, was it?

steps.player: Umm, no I guess not. Sorry about that.

options.text: There must be something down here that might help.

steps.player: There must be something down here that might help.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: I'm afraid I have no idea! It's a long way down as I said, so I can't see much from way up here!

steps.player: I'm telling you, it's really not that high.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Lies! Lies! Now can you see anything down there that might help, old chicken?

steps.player: Not really, no.

options.text: I could ask the princess!

steps.player: I could ask the princess!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Hang on, old underpants!...you're going to ask the princess to help you climb up this wall to see her prisoner.

steps.player: You know, on second thought maybe that's not such a good idea after all.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: No, indeed. Indeed, no.

steps.player: Well, I could try and ask her to let you out, perhaps? You know, get her to listen to reason.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Reason, eh? Hmmm. Well you could give that a try.

options.text: I could try speaking to the princess.

steps.player: I could try speaking to the princess.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Well, I suppose it wouldn't hurt to try, old socks! What would you say?

steps.player: Well, I could try and get her to listen to reason, I suppose.

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Reason, eh? Hmmm. Well, you could give that a try.

options.text: I could kill the princess for you!

steps.player: I could kill the princess for you!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: What? Kill the princess?

steps.player: Sure, she doesn't look so tough!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: What ever has gotten into your head, old war wound? Kill the princess. No, no, no. We don't do that sort of thing round here.

steps.player: But she's kidnapped you. Surely that makes her evil?

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Well, yes of course. In a manner of speaking, yes. But...but that still doesn't give us the right to go around lopping people's heads off because they're not very nice!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: No, there must be another way! Keep thinking!

steps.player: Ok...
But it would have been fun though, wouldn't it? Haha!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Hmmm.

steps.player: She would never have seen it coming! Blam!

steps.speaker: Drain pipe
steps.text: Yes, I get the idea. Now be a sport and think of a better idea!

steps.player: Right!

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.text: Yes? Please make it quick, I am waiting for someone.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.player: Oh, really? Who are you waiting for? Maybe I've met them?

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.text: You think so? Ha! Although you'd most likely remember if you had met this person. If you must know, I am waiting for a relative of mine to arrive.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.player: Oh, okay. Can I ask you something?
I notice you have a dwarf in the tower here. I was wondering why he is locked in there?

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.text: You are a nosy young person! Well, if you must know, he's in there because I have caught him for someone.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.text: I am not at liberty to say. In any case, this dwarf was caught spying and snooping and that sort of thing is not taken lightly.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.player: But he seems like a very nice person to me. A bit odd perhaps, but couldn't you let him go?

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.text: No, I don't think so. I will be nicely rewarded for catching him.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.text: Hmm, well as you asked nicely. Ok then.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.speaker: Miazrqa
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-miazrqa-a.text: No! Now please leave. You're annoying me!

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-th.speaker: Drain pipe
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-th.text: Eh? What? Oh! You don't have to use that anymore, old spoon! Climb up to speak to me!

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-th.speaker: Drain pipe
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-th.text: Up my beard of course! It was your idea after all, old spinach.

entering-the-tower-climbing-up-rupert-s-.text: You nimbly scale up the beard to the top of the tower.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.text: Aha! You made it. Well done, old sausage!

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.player: Yes, it was quite a climb, but you have a very strong beard.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.text: Indeed I do. Indeed I do.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.player: So, what can I help you with?

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.text: Ah! Straight to the point, eh, what? Good show old carrot, good show. Now let me explain.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.text: I'm in a bit of a fix right now. You see, the princess down there has this horrible relative who happens to be a witch.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.player: A witch? Let me guess, would this witch be her evil stepmother?

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.text: Stepmother? Ho! Good lord, no. No king in his right mind would marry a hag like that! No, this is her evil second-cousin, twice-removed.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.text: Right, well a young gnome friend of mine by the name of Winkin recently disappeared whilst delivering ogleroots to the market in Draynor.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.text: I don't know exactly, but someone told me he was last seen talking to a witch before he disappeared.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.player: Ok, so how can I help?

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.text: My investigations brought me to our friend the princess down there, old pinata. She's related to this witch, as I mentioned. I was...you know...showing a bit of interest in her to get her to give me information.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.text: She invited me back to her 'tower', saying she would tell me all I wanted to know, and then as I walked in the door she slammed it shut behind me.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.text: Yes, indeed! Rude indeed! Then, as I was hammering on the door I heard a hissing sound and smelt something strange. The next thing I remember is waking up to find my armour gone!

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.text: That wench must have taken it!

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.player: Ok, let me go and talk to her for you, then.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-in.text: Excellent! Good show, old spice! Off you go then.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-ag.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-ag.text: Ahh, you're back. Have you spoken to the princess yet, old mushroom?

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-ag.player: Oh, no I haven't had a chance yet. I'll be back when I have.

entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-ag.speaker: Rupert the Beard
entering-the-tower-speaking-to-rupert-ag.text: Right you are then, old chestnut.

entering-the-tower-attempting-to-leave-t.text: The trapdoor is locked. You can hear a clinking sound as you pull on it. You figure it must be connected to a mechanism of some sort through the tower.

entering-the-tower-climbing-down-rupert-.text: You nimbly scale back down the beard to the floor below.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant.text: Ah! What nice manners. It's so hard to find decently mannered young people these days. My name is Princess Miazrqa.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant.player: Pleased to meet you, Princess Miarz... er... Mizaz... Miquipzi... Marzipan?

options.text: That's an unusual name. Where is it from?

steps.player: That's an unusual name. Where is it from?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: My birth certificate. Now. how can I be of help?

options.text: I see there is an embarrassed-looking dwarf...

steps.player: I see there is an embarrassed-looking dwarf in the tower there.

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Yes, that's right. I'm waiting for him to be collected by someone.

options.text: Your first-cousin, once removed?

steps.player: Your first-cousin, once removed?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: No. You shouldn't guess answers like that. It's not very becoming. She is my second-cousin, twice removed and she is also a very powerful witch who could turn you into something nasty!

steps.player: Gosh! Sorry, please continue.

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Now as I was saying, my second-cousin, twice-removed is coming to collect the dwarf. She will find out why he's been snooping around. She has most...persuasive methods.

steps.player: Yes, that's actually why I came to speak with you. I was wondering if you couldn't let Rupert go? He's a nice fellow and I can't think he'd have done anything wrong.

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Ha! That won't matter to my cousin. She values her privacy above all else, you see.

steps.player: Surely there must be something that will change your mind? Is there anything you want?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Hmmm...well I suppose there is something you can do for me that might make me change my mind.

steps.player: Ok, what's that?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: I was at my second-cousin's house just the other day when I suddenly dropped a very valuable pendant that I was wearing. The chain must have broken, you see.

steps.player: Ok, go on.

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Well, no sooner had it touched the ground when all of a sudden a mouse ran out from a hole in the wall. It took my pendant in its teeth and disappeared back inside its hole.

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: As I'm sure you will believe, I was most upset as the pendant was a gift from my mother. I simply must get it back somehow.

steps.player: So you would like me to find it for you?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Oh, yes please! It means so much to me. If you are able to find the pendant for me, I will let your dwarf friend go.

steps.player: Very well. I will find it for you.

options.text: Where is your second-cousin's house?

steps.player: Where is your second-cousin's house?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: It's not far to the west of here, in Taverley village. It has a beautiful long garden - you can't miss it!

steps.player: Hey! I do know that house! I rescued some little kid's ball from there!

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: That was you? Oh, my cousin was absolutely furious when she found out about that! She went on about it for ages and even made her hair turn a quite ghastly green colour!

steps.player: Oh dear.

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Well I suggest you be extra careful when you look for my pendant then.

options.text: What does your pendant look like?

steps.player: What does your pendant look like?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: It's a lovely gold pendant.

steps.player: Is it particularly valuable?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Only to me really. It's not worth much and isn't magical, but it has a lot of sentimental value. It was my mother's pendant. She gave it to me on my tenth birthday.

options.text: Where are you the princess of exactly?

steps.player: Where are you the princess of exactly?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: I am the daughter of a great and powerful king. In a land far, far away.

steps.player: How far, exactly?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Far, far.

steps.player: Oh. What's the place called?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Asgarnia.

steps.player: Asgarnia? Aren't we in Asgarnia?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Well...yes. I suppose, but that doesn't mean it's not far, far away from somewhere else.

steps.player: Uh...I see.

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: I am the great niece of King Vallance himself.

steps.player: How impressive!

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Yes, it is, isn't it? Now was there anything else?

options.text: I need a key for the house.

steps.player: I need a key for the house.

steps.text: If the player doesn't own the Door key

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Of course. You may have one of my spare keys.
Door key

steps.player: Thanks very much.

steps.text: If the player already has the key

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Don't be silly. You have one already in your bag. Goodness me, how ever will you find my pendant with a memory like that?

steps.player: Ah, yes. Sorry.

options.text: I should be off, I think.

steps.player: I should be off, I think.

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Very well. Good luck with finding my pendant.

options.text: Your second-cousin, once removed?

steps.player: Your second-cousin, once removed?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: No. You shouldn't guess answers like that. It's not very becoming. She is my second-cousin, twice removed and she is also a very powerful witch who could turn you into something nasty!

options.text: Your first-cousin, twice removed?

steps.player: Your first-cousin, twice removed?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: No. You shouldn't guess answers like that. It's not very becoming. She is my second-cousin, twice removed and she is also a very powerful witch who could turn you into something nasty!

options.text: Your second-cousin, twice removed?

steps.player: Your second-cousin, twice removed?

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: Why, yes! That was a very clever guess indeed! She's actually a very powerful witch. Now allow me to reward you in some way as I am feeling generous.

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: As I said, my cousin is a witch but she is also a lover of music. She has a lovely gramophone and she keeps a piano in her basement - why? I have no idea - but you may find it interesting to examine.

steps.player: What's so special about it? I've seen pianos all over the place.

steps.speaker: Miazrqa
steps.text: I don't really know. I know my cousin goes on about that piano a lot, but I've played on it many times and I can't figure out why she likes it so much.

steps.player: I see. Thank you for that...er...useful knowledge.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.player: Please can you repeat that last bit? A flock of noisy birds flew overhead there and I couldn't hear you.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: I see. How ghastly. Let me continue.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: Now as I was saying, my second-cousin, twice-removed is coming to collect the dwarf. She will find out why he's been snooping around. She has most...persuasive methods.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.player: I just have another question before I look for your pendant.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: If you must, but you are wasting time.

options.text: Where is your second-cousin's house?
What does your pendant look like?
Where are you the princess of exactly?
I need a key for the house.
I should be off, I think.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Rupert
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: Ah! Welcome back, old curtains! How did it go with the old princess down there? Did she agree to let me out?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.player: Sort of. She's asked me to do something for her first.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Rupert
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: Oh, right. What was it then, old parrot?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.player: I have to find a gold pendant of hers that she lost in that witch's house in Taverley.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Rupert
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: By all the gods! You have to go in there? You must be careful, [player name]. She's a wily one that witch, from what I've heard. No doubt there's all sorts of weird magics over there!

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.player: Don't worry. I'll be careful. I've been in there once before, so I know what's there.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Rupert
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: You've been in there? Goodness me! What did you see? Did you see a gnome in there anywhere?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.player: I don't think so. I'm sure I would have remembered. I was looking for a ball for a boy who had lost it in the witch's garden.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Rupert
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: Hmm, he was probably lucky that was all he lost with all that weird magic going on, eh?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.player: Yes, quite. I'll see what I can find out though.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Rupert
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: Ah! Good show, old kebab! I'll wait here for you. But don't be long. Who knows what that princess will do to me next!

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-playing-th.text: A compartment opens in the piano. It looks like you found the right tune.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-searching-.text: You find what appears to be a To-Do list for the day, some sort of odd potion recipe and what can only be described as a shrunken vegetable of some sort.
Shrinking recipe, To-do list and 2 Shrunk ogleroot
There are no more shrunken ogleroots in here. You'll have to find one somewhere else.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-mixing-the.text: The potion swirls and steams within the vial. It looks almost as if it is trying to make itself smaller as you look at it...

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-upon-enter.text: You sense a strange magical aura around you as you enter this room.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-drinking-t.text: The player shrinks and enters the mouse hole.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-taking-the.text: You take the pendant. It shrinks in your hand as you touch it.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: Ah! [player name], old pantaloons! Good to see you, good to see you. What news?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.player: Princess Miazrqa has agreed to free you.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: Princess Marzipan, eh? What a mouthful.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: Ah, I see. Good show. Say, did you find out anything about my missing friend?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.player: I did, I think. But it's not good news. The witch has your friend locked up in a cage, down under the house itself.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: Good gods! That's awful! I won't have all this kidnapping nonsense! And to think we're supposed to be a civilised land!

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: I'll think of something. In the meantime, you still need to get me out of here. Maybe you should see if Miazrqa is ready to let me out.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.player: I found your pendant, Princess Miazrqa!

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.text: Oh, how wonderful! I'm so grateful.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.player: Umm, your second-cousin has some very strange...creatures she keeps.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.text: Oh yes. Those are her little darlings. I shudder to think what she might do if something were to happen to any of them.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.text: Oh yes. Why, only last month one of them got out for a wander and some horrid farmer attacked it with his ear!

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.text: Indeed! Tried to choke the poor thing with it. Anyway, my cousin went into a frightful rage and turned that wretched farmer into one of his own chickens. We had a lovely roast meal that day. Happy memories...

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.player: I think I feel a little ill...

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.text: Oh dear, I hope you're not coming down with something.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.text: Now, can I have the pendant please?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.player: Will you agree to let Rupert go free?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.text: Of course. The pendant means more to me than anything.
Cutscene with Rupert looking for his armour as he descends the tower

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.text: By Saradomin! My armour was on the stairs up there!

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-returning-.text: Aha! Sweet freedom! It's good to be alive, old sweet shop! Thank you for freeing me, [player name].

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.text: (Player automatically walks up to Rupert after the cutscene.)

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.text: Thank you, [player name]. You've done a great service for me and all the dwarves and gnomes.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.player: I'm just happy I could help...hey! What happened to your long beard? Where did it go?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.text: Hah! Don't fret, old penny whistle! It's still here. The front of my armour was specially crafted to allow my beard to fold up inside. Do you see?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.player: Oh yes! I can see it now. That's pretty clever!

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.text: Indeed it is, old cheese! Now allow me to reward you in some way. All I have is my armour, but you are welcome to take any piece of it that you wish.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.player: Please could I have the helmet?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.text: Of course, of course. Here you go, old pumpkin.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.player: So what will you be doing now, Rupert?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-speaking-w.text: Thanks to you I can carry on my investigations. Good show, old brussels sprout!

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.player: Princess Miazrqa, I found out what your cousin is up to.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.text: Really? You know, I have always wondered. She's ever so secretive and never tells me anything. I was hoping she might tell me when I saw her next.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.player: So you didn't know that she kidnaps poor defenceless gnomes?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.text: What?! Never! That's absolutely awful! How could she? Oh, that's just so...so...mean!

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.text: It's quite hard to believe. Do you have any proof?

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.player: Yes. There is a gnome in her basement right now!

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.text: How horrid! Well, when I see her I will tell her exactly what I think. Thank you for telling me all this, [player name].

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.player: You know, Rupert - the dwarf here - is trying to put a stop to what is going on. I am sure he could use your help.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-miazrqa-s-.text: Really? You may tell him that I will help him in any way I can.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-rupert-s-r.player: Rupert, I told Miazrqa about what the witch was doing and she was horrified by it.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-rupert-s-r.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-rupert-s-r.text: I'm not surprised, old kiwi. It's a pretty ghastly business with all this kidnapping gnomes and dwarves.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-rupert-s-r.player: Yes. Miazrqa has said she would like to help you with your investigations and that you can use this tower as your base of operations if you want.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-rupert-s-r.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-rupert-s-r.text: Really? That's just fantastic! You are certainly full of surprises, [player name]. Good show!

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-rupert-s-r.player: Well, I had better be going for now. Good luck.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-rupert-s-r.speaker: Rupert the Beard
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-rupert-s-r.text: And to you, my friend. And to you.

looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.speaker: Miazrqa
looking-for-miazrqa-s-pendant-talking-to.text: Thanks again for finding my pendant. I felt so lost without it.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: I managed to get Rupert's helmet for you.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Excellent, [player name]! I'll take that as well. I hope all this work wasn't too difficult.
Rupert's helmet

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: Difficult? You have no idea! There were huge creatures trying to eat me, other creatures trying to tear me apart, witches, gnomes in distress, princesses, and I had to deal with them all!

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Goodness me! I'm glad I sent you instead of going myself.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Er...I mean...I knew sending you was the right thing to do. I was sure you could handle anything that came up. Now then, the beans...

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: Yes, that's what all this was about wasn't it? Some beans! They must be worth a lot for this much trouble!

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Actually, the beans are almost worthless.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: Worthless? So why did I go to all of this trouble for you? I'm not particularly happy about that.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Calm down, my young, hot-headed friend. There was a good reason for getting these beans.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Now that you have proven yourself worthy of being a competent and trustworthy treasure collector, I can tell the real use for the beans.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: As I said before, these beans are magical. There is a specially prepared mound of earth to the south-east of Taverley.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Plant the beans there and then be sure to water them well. You will need to have some knowledge of farming for this.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: Ok, so then what do I do?

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: When the beans are planted and watered, they will grow into an enormous plant of some sort. I'm not sure what exactly. At the top of this plant is our prize.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: Our prize? What exactly is this prize?

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: The ultimate collectible item, my dear friend. It is rumoured that in a land of clouds where none dare to tread lest they plummet to the earth, lies a goblin made of gold...

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Yes. Yes, indeed! A golden goblin. Legend tells of a time when goblins discovered gold in an abandoned dwarf mine and began to mine and smelt it. What for, nobody knows. Something evil, I'd wager.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: The goblins produced great smelting works, overseen by a particularly smart goblin with a head for business. Gubblebak was his name. He was shrewd, cunning and he loved gold...

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: He worked his fellow goblins day and night to produce more and more gold, until finally they could stand his hard labour no more and they mutinied.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: That's right. They turned on him. No-one is sure about the exact events, but somehow Gubblebak fell into one of the smelting pots of liquid gold.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Well now, goblins are tough little creatures and he managed to somehow crawl out of the pot covered in hot, molten gold.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: He was smart indeed, but even smart people do foolish things. He threw himself into a nearby water trough.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: But surely that's what anyone would have done? Why is that a bad thing?

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Ahh, well you see...when you take hot liquid metal and cool it instantly, it becomes rock hard straight away. That's how blacksmiths make their weapons and armour.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: Oh, I see. So Gubblebak became hard as a rock?

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: That's right. And that's the way he stayed ever afterwards. So the legend says, at least. And the cloud area will be waiting for you when you have planted the beans to find this golden goblin.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: So let me see if I have this straight.

I need to plant the beans in an earth mound south-east of here, water them, let them grow into some big plant and then climb the plant to get to a cloudy area, find a golden goblin and bring it back to you?

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Exactly right! You've got it. Now did I mention about the giant?

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Yes, that's right. The giant.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: No, I'm pretty sure you didn't mention any giants! What giant? Now would be a good time to mention it if you were going to!

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Oh right, sorry. Must have slipped my mind. There's a bit of a large-ish giant up there. Uh...shouldn't be anything to worry about. But...uh...I think he might have the goblin, you see.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: So how exactly do I get the goblin then?

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Well, you're probably going to have to kill him for it. But...but a big strong adventurer like yourself shouldn't have any trouble whatsoever with that, I'm sure!

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Here are the beans as promised.
Magic beans

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: Ok then, to recap. I need to plant the beans over there, water them, let them grow into some big plant, climb the plant to get to a cloudy area, kill a giant, find a golden goblin and bring it back to you?

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.text: Oh, well done! You do pay attention! Good luck!

getting-sylas-magic-bean-returning-to-sy.player: Thanks...I think I'm going to need it.

getting-sylas-magic-bean-asking-sylas-ab.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-asking-sylas-ab.text: So then. Do you want to run through what you need to do for me again?

getting-sylas-magic-bean-asking-sylas-ab.player: Ok then, to recap: I need to plant the beans, water them, let them grow into some big plant, climb the plant to get to a cloudy area, kill a giant, find a golden goblin and bring it back to you?

getting-sylas-magic-bean-asking-sylas-ab.speaker: Sylas
getting-sylas-magic-bean-asking-sylas-ab.text: Oh, well done! You do pay attention! Good luck!

the-final-battle-reading-the-signpost-ne.text: There is more writing on the sign. It reads: 'This earth mound has been magically prepared. Please keep off. Farming strictly prohibited. You have been warned!'

the-final-battle-watering-the-mound-befo.text: You succeed in making the ground a little muddy...but not much else.

the-final-battle-planting-the-bean-in-th.text: You plant the beans in the dry ground. Perhaps you should give them some water as well.

the-final-battle-watering-the-bean-mound.text: A cutscene shows the bean growing into a giant beanstalk.
You sense something about to happen...
(Player waters the soil and it immediately grows into a giant beanstalk.)

the-final-battle-talking-to-sylas-after-.player: I've grown the beans into a huge stalk, as you asked. What am I supposed to do now?

the-final-battle-talking-to-sylas-after-.speaker: Sylas
the-final-battle-talking-to-sylas-after-.text: Hmm, have you climbed up the stalk yet?

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: Yes.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Very well. Did you find the giant?

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: Yes.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Right then. Did you defeat him and find the golden goblin?

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: Yes.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Excellent! Well done. Now bring me the golden goblin and we're almost done.

steps.player: Umm...what happens if I forget to pick up the golden goblin after defeating the giant and leave?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Well, I expect it will still be waiting up there for you when you go back up. It's highly unlikely anyone would risk going up there to steal it.

steps.player: Ok, thanks.

options.text: No.

steps.player: No.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Right then, that's your next task. You will need to defeat that giant to get the golden goblin from him.

options.text: No.

steps.player: No.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: He wasn't there? This is highly irregular. Are you sure you looked properly? I expect he'd be hard to miss.

steps.player: I'll go and have another look.

options.text: No.

steps.player: No.

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: Right, then you will need to climb the stalk and find the golden goblin for me.

steps.player: Where can I find it?

steps.speaker: Sylas
steps.text: I think a big giant has it at the top of the stalk. You will need to get it from him.

steps.player: Right. I'm on my way.

the-final-battle-the-battle-with-glod.text: Early during fight, only happens once:

steps.speaker: Glod
steps.text: Gods, give Glod strength!
Glod appears to have more Strength and Attack power than before!

steps.speaker: Glod
steps.text: Flee, pesky mortal!
At Glod's cry you are forced to run away!

steps.speaker: Glod
steps.text: You puny human. Come to Glod!
You are enraged by Glod's taunts and forced to charge towards him to fight!

steps.speaker: Glod
steps.text: GLOD SMASH!
Your prayer is drained by Glod's attack!

steps.speaker: Glod
steps.text: Glod not die so easily!
Gold heals himself slightly.

the-final-battle-speaking-to-sylas-after.player: Sylas! I found the golden goblin!

the-final-battle-speaking-to-sylas-after.speaker: Sylas
the-final-battle-speaking-to-sylas-after.text: Excellent work, Player! Now, that giant will likely have friends. It is too dangerous to leave that stalk up there like that.

the-final-battle-speaking-to-sylas-after.player: Ok, so what should we do?

the-final-battle-speaking-to-sylas-after.speaker: Sylas
the-final-battle-speaking-to-sylas-after.text: First, let me take that goblin from you. Next we need to cut down that beanstalk as soon as possible. I hope you're a good woodcutter!

the-final-battle-speaking-to-sylas-after.speaker: Sylas
the-final-battle-speaking-to-sylas-after.text: Find an axe. Any axe should do. Then cut down that stalk as soon as you can before another giant finds out what you have done and comes for us!

the-final-battle-asking-sylas-how-to-cut.player: Can you remind me what I am doing now?

the-final-battle-asking-sylas-how-to-cut.speaker: Sylas
the-final-battle-asking-sylas-how-to-cut.text: You've forgotten already? Did you get hit on the head by that giant? Do you have amnesia?

the-final-battle-asking-sylas-how-to-cut.player: No, I just can't remember what I am supposed to do.

the-final-battle-asking-sylas-how-to-cut.speaker: Sylas
the-final-battle-asking-sylas-how-to-cut.text: Find an axe. Any axe should do. Then cut down that stalk as soon as you can before another giant finds out what you have done and comes for us!

finishing-the-quest-trying-to-climb-back.text: You've given the Golden Goblin to Sylas already. You don't think going back up there would be prudent!

finishing-the-quest-trying-to-chop-down-.text: You will need an axe to cut down the beanstalk.

finishing-the-quest-chopping-the-beansta.text: The beanstalk is too thick for you to cut through. Perhaps there is a way of making it thinner?

finishing-the-quest-shrinking-the-beanst.text: A cutscene shows the beanstalk shrinking to normal size.
You sense something about to happen...
(Player pours the shrinking potion on the beanstalk.)

finishing-the-quest-chopping-down-the-be.text: A cutscene shows the beanstalk being chopped down.
You attempt to cut the beanstalk down...

finishing-the-quest-using-axe-on-the-sta.text: You have already cut the beanstalk down.

finishing-the-quest-using-any-item-besid.text: You decide that doing that would not be the most prudent of actions.

finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.speaker: Sylas
finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.text: Have you cut down the stalk?

finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.speaker: Sylas
finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.text: Good work, [player name]! At last we can relax. We've completed our task and you have done me a great service!

finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.speaker: Sylas
finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.text: Now, let me reward you. You may have wondered what possible use I could have had for Rupert's helmet.

finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.player: It did indeed seem like an odd item to look for.

finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.speaker: Sylas
finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.text: Ah, yes! However, tucked inside the helmet is a tiny bottle with a very special potion. It was made by a witch, here in Taverley, but Rupert must have found it.

finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.speaker: Sylas
finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.text: Not knowing what the potion was, he simply tucked it away in his helmet.

finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.player: Not more potions?! I've had enough of potions for now.

finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.speaker: Sylas
finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.text: Relax, my friend. This potion is almost harmless. It is actually a particularly strong hair-tonic.

finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.player: Oh! Well, that would explain Rupert's beard then.

finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.speaker: Sylas
finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.text: Yes, indeed! I also imagine poor Rupert never understood why his beard grew so alarmingly fast. Poor lad.

finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.speaker: Sylas
finishing-the-quest-finishing-up.text: Anyway, I have removed the potion now and you may keep the helmet along with your rewards. Don't worry, it's quite harmless and the helmet should help you in your adventures.

finishing-the-quest-talking-to-sylas-wit.speaker: Sylas
finishing-the-quest-talking-to-sylas-wit.text: Have you cut down the stalk?

finishing-the-quest-talking-to-sylas-wit.speaker: Sylas
finishing-the-quest-talking-to-sylas-wit.text: Great work, [player name]. Now, I have something for you, but you're going to need a space in your inventory. Speak to me again when you have made some room.
